newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-HEAT FORCES CLOSURE OF MELBOURNE CENTRE COURT ROOF.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HEAT FORCES CLOSURE OF MELBOURNE CENTRE COURT ROOF.

text.p: Australian Open officials on Tuesday ordered the closure of Melbourne Park's Centre Court roof as weather forecasters predicted a third straight day of intense heat.

The stadium's retractable roof was drawn shut on Tuesday morning, shortly before quarter-final action began in what forecasters said would be another day of over 40 degree Celsius (104 Fahrenheit) heat.
"In the interest of players and spectators the decision has been made to close the roof," tournament referee Peter Bellenger said in a statement.

Bellenger had been under pressure on Monday to close the roof over the Centre Court, and even reschedule matches on outside courts, as players complained of feeling like being in an oven and experts warned of serious health risks.
But Bellenger stood firm until Tuesday, implying that he could not have closed the roof any earlier without prejudicing players who were scheduled to meet on outside show courts.

"The tournament referee has the option to close the roof from today -- the start of the maindraw singles quarter finals onwards -- because all players will be playing on the Centre Court under ideal conditions," Bellenger's statement said.
But the referee's ruling came as no comfort to the Open doubles and junior tournament players who will still have to brave the searing heat on outside courts on Tuesday.
"Play on outside matches will continue as scheduled," Bellenger said.

Players and medical experts have warned that competitors risk extreme dehydration and perhaps death while playing in the intense heat felt on Monday when on-court temperatures topped 50 degrees Celsius (122 Fahrenheit) for a second straight day.
"It could be just a matter of time before someone dies out there," Australian Medical Association spokesman Dr Gerald Segal was quoted as saying in the Herald-Sun newspaper on Tuesday.

Trainers were kept busy attending to stressed players on Monday, the hottest day of the tournament so far, despite efforts by Open officials to alleviate the heat by providing fans and iced towels to players during breaks in play.
